title: Your Eyes Read Words You Swear Were Blank, Yet One 300-Millisecond Wave Sparks Awareness

acts.name: 2006 Paris Masked-Word Paradigm & Consciousness Switch
sentences: Your eyes spot hidden words while you see a blank screen!
Yet one tiny timing step turns awareness wide awake!
This is the true story of the Global Workspace Experiment.
Here is what went wrong with old views of awareness.
For decades, brain researchers called consciousness too vague to measure.
In two thousand six, Stanislas Dehaene built a clean Paris test.
Words flashed for forty-three milliseconds, like a quick finger snap.
Right behind each flashed word came a scrambled mask.
One dial moved that mask — and that wasn't the strangest part.

acts.name: Subliminal 33-ms Visual Decoding vs All-or-None 50-ms Threshold
sentences: At thirty-three milliseconds, like a film frame, screens looked blank.
Did that unseen word stop at their eyes?
Sensors caught a wave for two hundred milliseconds, like a whisper.
The visual cortex, your vision center, decoded every single letter!
Word meaning stirred backstage, then faded out.
Past fifty milliseconds, like a tipping domino, everything flipped.
Did sight fade in slowly or snap on?
Sight jumped from zero to one hundred percent, like a wall switch.
Watching your brain read unseen words was a total nightmare.

acts.name: 300-Millisecond Parietal-Prefrontal Global Workspace Ignition
sentences: What turns a silent visual spark into waking thought?
At three hundred milliseconds, like a relay baton, ignition hit.
Signals unlocked the parietal cortex, your attention spotlight.
Instead of fading, the prefrontal cortex, your planner, fired back.
That Paris team named this the global workspace.
One thought echoed everywhere, like a stadium loudspeaker.
Then your speech hubs could report that word aloud.
Their team also split weak flashes from strong ignored views.
But here's the twist: could this wave spot hidden minds?

acts.name: Bedside Coma Awareness Detection & COGITATE Open-Science Bet
sentences: In Paris clinics, brain-injury patients could not move.
Doctors tracked that three-hundred-millisecond wave, like a sonar ping.
When front and back shared signals, hidden minds were awake!
Families learned silent patients still heard them.
Yet did everyone accept that workspace model?
Rival scientists placed awareness inside rear brain hubs.
Both rivals signed an open bet before testing began.
What happened when labs tested both rivals together?

acts.name: 2025 Nature 256-Volunteer Adversarial Showdown
sentences: In twenty twenty-five, teams scanned two hundred fifty-six people, like a full theater.
That landmark open test challenged claims on both sides!
Starting waves held strong, yet ending bursts stayed quiet.
And the rival rear-brain theory missed steady waves.
Neither rival won everything — open data won instead.
The researchers were left completely stunned.
Consciousness graduated from armchair talk to hard science.
One shared experiment pushed brain mysteries forward!

acts.name: Protecting Your Single-Broadcast 300-ms Conscious Stage
sentences: What does your global workspace mean for your focus today?
Your visual cortex, your vision center, runs quiet tasks backstage.
Yet your prefrontal cortex, your planner, shares one rich thought.
Spot one alert, and for three hundred milliseconds, like a turnstile, others wait.
Running three open tasks jams that single broadcast stage.
Silence phone alerts and give one deep problem the stage.
Unbroken quiet focus lets one idea link memory and speech.
Which proves your brain works backstage — yet broadcasts one conscious thought.
